newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ruffled EMU feathers to keep OLOs on their toes.
newsitem.headline: Ruffled EMU feathers to keep OLOs on their toes.

text.p: Belgian government bonds (OLOs) and futures benefitted from a lull in the verbal storms raging over the euro and related convergence and EMU-entry criteria, but there was little conviction in the gains, dealers said.
"Pre-Amsterdam, everybody will be cautious," a trader said. Buyers were seen at the long end of the curve on Wednesday, sellers at the short end, but volumes were low.

"It is reasonably difficult to give a strategy for this market...yields are very low already...now is not the time to buy," another trader said. She added investors might want to wait for six-percent yields on benchmark 10-year paper.
However, she was not sure that level would be seen this week. The benchmark 2007 OLO BE286= yielded 5.84 percent at 1040 GMT, down a tick from Tuesday's close.

The focus for the rest of the week might shift to the U.S. where retail sales data for May are eagerly awaited. They are expected to show strength and, if in line with forecasts, could rekindle speculation on a Fed interest rate hike in July.
The figures are due on Thursday US-ECI.
Another trader said the EMU squabbles were underscoring a lack of attraction of European bonds to the average U.S. investor, but there were no clear flows across the Atlantic.

One trader said he did not foresee much of a softening of the EMU criteria resulting from a new, social, paragraph in the stability pact. "Anything in the paragraph will not really be binding, besides, it will be hard to lay down very specific targets on job creation."
No money would be committed to the fight for more jobs so that in that sense there were no threats to deficits or debt, and no implications for inflation, he added.
Only a delay to EMU might force markets to re-think its attitude to EMU and unwind convergence trades. The strong pro-EMU political will makes that unlikely, he said.
Markets are in the ban of EMU, a trader said, noting several EU leaders would meet later today. A speech by German Finance Minister Waigel this afternoon will be scrutinised DE-EMU.

"Markets are discounting a broad and soft EMU, while waiting for the outcome of next week's Amsterdam summit," an analyst said. Attention will focus on efforts by the new French government to have the post-euro stability pact, complemented with pledges on fighting unemployment, ratified in Amsterdam.
"EMU sentiment is the primary mover for longer-dated OLOs -- likely to be more positive today as statements out of France suggest potential for agreement at the Amsterdam summit."
